title: Pullback naturality of the canonical cover SES boundary
statement: For any morphism g prime:X prime to X of schemes with derived module categories, any two-open cover X=U union V, any K,K prime and psi:Lg prime star K to K prime, use exactly the concrete SES boundaries and adjunction-compatible shifts of [def-pc-rf-mv-canonical-ses-shifts]. On X prime, the image of the source boundary under Lg prime star, followed by its constructed shift and psi[1], equals the canonical overlap base-change map for the open inclusion followed by the target SES boundary. The overlap map is the pinned base-change comparison followed by the inverse pullback/open-restriction comparison and restriction of psi, as constructed in [def-pc-rf-mv-base-change-components]. No subsequent f prime direct image or comparison on S prime occurs.

source.place: Tags 08BV and 08HY; Tag 0DJ9 induction diagram, the boundary square before applying the subsequent direct image

proof.text: Identify mvCanonicalBoundary with schemeMVBoundary using canonical_boundary_eq for the overlap U intersection V. The existing canonicalMV_spec supplies naturality for any derived morphism K to L, so canonical boundary naturality follows by rewriting both endpoints.

Set alpha to the pinned g adjunction transpose of psi. Apply the proved direct-image boundary comparison to Kprime and its inverse-image cover. This gives Rg(delta prime) followed by the fixed right-derived shift equals c hom followed by the boundary of Rg(Kprime). Ordinary boundary naturality gives delta followed by alpha[1] equals overlap-restriction of alpha followed by that same boundary.

The single-open transposition lemma identifies the transpose of the displayed overlap component with overlap-restriction of alpha followed by c inverse. Apply injectivity of the pinned g Hom equivalence and postcompose with the invertible right-derived shift comparison. Hom-equivalence naturality on both sides, mvCanonicalHomEquiv_shift, the two preceding boundary equations and c inverse times c hom cancel to give the desired equality. The private boundary_pullback_of_transpose theorem proves this categorical algebra in Lean.
